questions.question: Rajashree Shirke was awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi for her contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
Rajashree Shirke is a prominent Kathak dancer, researcher, and choreographer known for her expertise in the Lucknow Gharana.
  • Contribution: She is celebrated for her 'Kathayakary' technique, which blends storytelling with the technical brilliance of Kathak.
  • Recognition: She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her immense contribution to the preservation and innovation of this North Indian classical dance.

questions.question: T Balasaraswati, who was a dancer and actress, used to perform which of the following classical dances of India?
questions.solution:
Tanjore Balasaraswati was a legendary dancer and actress who popularized Bharatanatyam globally.
  • Heritage: She belonged to a family of traditional temple musicians and dancers (Devadasis) and was a revolutionary in bringing the dance to the public stage.
  • Awards: She was honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1955) and the Padma Vibhushan (1977).

questions.question: In the monasteries of which state was the Sattriya dance form developed?
questions.solution:
The Sattriya dance form was developed and preserved in the Sattras (monasteries) of Assam.
  • Function: These Sattras were established by the saint Srimanta Sankardev as centers for religious and cultural activities.
  • Status: It was recognized as a Classical Dance of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in the year 2000.

questions.question: In which year did Indian dancer, Sonal Mansingh receive the Padma Vibhushan, India's second highest civilian award?
questions.solution:
In 2003, Sonal Mansingh became the youngest recipient of the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian honor.
  • Expertise: She is a master of both Bharatanatyam and Odissi.
  • Accolades: She was also the first woman dancer in India to be awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1992.

questions.question: The tribal dance, Kunbi, is predominantly performed in the Indian state of ________.
questions.solution:
Kunbi is a tribal folk dance predominantly performed by the Kunbi community in the state of Goa.
  • Context: It is a social dance performed mainly by women during festive occasions like Shigmo.
  • Style: It is characterized by simple yet rhythmic movements and reflects the earthy, agricultural lifestyle of the tribe.

questions.question: Who among the following is India's first transgender Bharatanatyam dancer and the first transgender woman to receive the Padma Shri in 2019 who was also a recipient of honorary doctorate for her contribution to the field of Bharatanatyam?
questions.solution:
Narthaki Nataraj is a historic figure in Indian arts, being the first transgender woman to receive the Padma Shri (2019).
  • Style: She is a specialist in the Thanjavur Nayaki Bhava tradition of Bharatanatyam.
  • Contribution: Her success has significantly improved the visibility and social standing of the transgender community in the field of classical arts.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities introduced the Sattriya dance in Assam?
questions.solution:
Srimanta Sankardev, a 15th-16th century polymath and saint, introduced Sattriya dance in Assam.
  • Movement: It was part of his Neo-Vaishnavite movement, designed to simplify religious teachings through Ankiya Naats (one-act plays).
  • Purpose: The dance was originally performed by celibate monks (Bhokots) in monasteries.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Sattriya dance form of India?
questions.solution:
The founder of Sattriya is the great saint-reformer Sankardev. (This reinforces his role as the architect of Assamese cultural identity).
  • Related Terms: He also created Borgeet (devotional songs) and the Bhaona (traditional theatre style).

questions.question: Padma Shri awardees in 2022, known for their great performances of the dance style of Kathak, sister duo Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana belong to which state?
questions.solution:
The sister duo Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana are distinguished Kathak dancers from Uttar Pradesh (specifically Agra).
  • Style: They are known for their Benaras Gharana style and their performances centered on the spiritual theme of Hori.
  • Honor: They were jointly awarded the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.question: Which dancer founded the Kalakshetra Institute in Chennai that promotes performing art forms?
questions.solution:
Rukmini Devi Arundale founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai in 1936.
  • Mission: The institute was created to revive the traditional Indian arts, particularly Bharatanatyam, and remove the social stigma attached to it.
  • Architecture: It follows a Gurukul-style education system and is recognized as an Institution of National Importance.

questions.question: Oli Jerang, a Sattriya dancer, belongs to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Oli Jerang is a noted Sattriya dancer who represents the state of Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Note: While Sattriya originated in Assam, it has practitioners across neighboring states; her contributions help in the regional promotion of the art form.

questions.question: T Balasaraswati, who received the Sangeet Natak Akademi and Padma Vibhushan award, was a _________ dancer.
questions.solution:
T Balasaraswati (repeating for reinforcement) was a premier Bharatanatyam dancer.
  • Note: She was famous for her exceptional Abhinaya (facial expressions) and her ability to perform long dance sequences while singing simultaneously.

questions.question: Bharati Shivaji, a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the Sahitya Kala Parishad Samman and Padmashri by the Government of India, was associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
Bharati Shivaji is a renowned artist credited with the revival and propagation of Mohiniyattam.
  • Achievement: She received the Padma Shri and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her research into the movements and costumes of this Kerala dance form.
  • Contribution: She helped bring Mohiniyattam out of the shadow of Kathakali and Bharatanatyam.

questions.question: Villu Pattu, where performers narrate stories through songs with the villu or bow as the main instrument, is a folk dance of:
questions.solution:
Villu Pattu (Bow Song) is an ancient form of musical storytelling from Tamil Nadu.
  • Instrument: The main instrument is a Villu (a long bow) with bells attached, which the lead performer strikes while narrating heroic or mythological tales.
  • Context: It is typically performed during village temple festivals (Kodai).

questions.question: Kathak dancer Birju Maharaj received India's second highest civilian honour, the Padma Vibhushan, in which year?
questions.solution:
The legendary Pandit Birju Maharaj was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1986.
  • Background: He was the leading light of the Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin Gharana of Kathak.
  • Skills: Beyond dancing, he was a superb singer, drummer (tabla/pakhawaj), and choreographer in world cinema.

questions.question: 'Abhinaya Darpana' by Nandikesvara is one of the main sources of textual material for the study of the technique and grammar of body movement in the __________dance.
questions.solution:
Abhinaya Darpana (The Mirror of Gesture) by Nandikesvara is a fundamental text for Bharatanatyam.
  • Content: It provides detailed instructions on Hasta Mudras (hand gestures), Pada Bhedas (feet positions), and facial expressions used in Indian classical dance.

questions.question: To which of the following Indian states does Mohiniattam classical dance form belong?
questions.solution:
Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that belongs to the state of Kerala.
  • Characteristics: It is characterized by graceful, swaying body movements and subtle facial expressions.
  • Etymology: It literally means the 'Dance of the Enchantress' (Mohini).

questions.question: Saroja Vaidyanathan, the recipient of Padma Shri in 2002 and Padma Bhushan in 2013 is a dancer of which classical dance form?
questions.solution:
Saroja Vaidyanathan was a prominent Bharatanatyam dancer, choreographer, and the founder of the 'Ganesa Natyalaya' in Delhi.
  • Honors: She received the Padma Shri (2002) and Padma Bhushan (2013).
  • Contribution: She was known for her simplified teaching methods and her books on the classical dance form.

questions.question: Sarayu Sai was given the Natya Kalajyoti Award in 2006 for which dance style?
questions.solution:
Sarayu Sai (also known as Sarayu Rao) is an acclaimed Bharatanatyam dancer who received the Natya Kalajyoti award.
  • Context: This award is given by the Shreyas Foundation to recognize excellence in the field of dance.

questions.question: CV Chandrasekhar, recipient of Padma Bhushan is a performer of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.solution:
C.V. Chandrasekhar is a legendary Bharatanatyam dancer, academician, and choreographer.
  • Recognition: He is a recipient of the Padma Bhushan (2011) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship.
  • Style: He is highly respected for his technical perfection and his long tenure as a professor at the Banaras Hindu University.

questions.question: Nritya Chudamani Award is given every year by which cultural institution to an artist of Indian classical dance style?
questions.solution:
The Nritya Chudamani award is presented annually by the Sri Krishna Gana Sabha, a premier cultural institution in Chennai.
  • Significance: It is one of the most prestigious titles given to a classical dancer during the December Music and Dance Season in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: The Kinnauris of _______________________ perform Losar Shona Chuksam, a Kinnauri dance.
questions.solution:
Losar Shona Chuksam is a traditional folk dance performed by the Kinnauri people of Himachal Pradesh.
  • Occasion: It is performed during the Losar (Tibetan New Year) festival.
  • Movement: The dance involves slow, rhythmic steps and is usually performed in a circular formation.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states is the annual Hampi Dance Utsav celebrated?
questions.solution:
The Hampi Dance Utsav (also known as Vijaya Utsav) is celebrated annually in Karnataka.
  • Venue: It takes place amidst the ruins of the ancient capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, Hampi (a UNESCO World Heritage site).
  • Purpose: The festival celebrates the grandeur of the bygone era through dance, music, and processions.

questions.question: Mudiyettu which was included in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, is a ritual dance drama of which state?
questions.solution:
Mudiyettu is a traditional ritual theatre and dance drama from Kerala.
  • Theme: It depicts the mythological battle between the Goddess Kali and the demon Darika.
  • UNESCO Status: It was inscribed on the Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee Kalamandalam Gopi is recognised globally as the face of which dance form?
questions.solution:
Kalamandalam Gopi is a world-renowned exponent of Kathakali from Kerala.
  • Specialty: He is famous for his Pacha (heroic/noble) roles, particularly as Nala and Karna.
  • Legacy: He is considered the face of Kathakali globally due to his emotional depth and rigorous adherence to the tradition.
